featureRef: 4.2 Issuing fee invoices at different scopes
name: Raise fee invoices against the approved structure, at school, class, section or student scope
priorityReason: The school's income begins here. Overdue tracking, reminders, late fees and reconciliation all read the invoices this raises.

goal.capability: to raise the fee bills for a period at whatever scope the office needs
goal.outcome: every family owes a correct, calculated amount they can see the workings of, and has been told

secondaryActors.involvement: Authorises a school-wide issue. A run of that size is not a routine act.
Receives the invoice at the point it is created and can open and print the challan.
Sees the resulting billed and outstanding figures.

additional.description: A monthly run raises the recurring invoices on the school's billing day.
A student is placed in a class, which makes them billable from that date.

preconditions.condition: An approved fee structure exists for the class, effective for the billing period.
Students in scope are placed in a class and section and are active for the academic session.

establishedBy.name: Class placement of an admitted student

preconditions.condition: An authenticated session exists and the acting user is Accounts or School Admin.
A chart of accounts exists, so each invoice and its tax can post to the ledger.

establishedBy.name: Reading the books: ledger, trial balance and journals

preconditions.condition: Where withholding tax applies, the tax rate and the household threshold are configured.

postConditions: One invoice exists per student in scope, at status Issued, with a unique number and its own calculated amount.

Every adjustment that produced the figure — concession, credit applied, installment split, late fee carried and withholding tax — is a separate line on the invoice and on the challan, so a family can see the workings and not just the total.
Any credit held against the family code has been drawn down by what was applied, and the remainder is still held for the next bill.
Each invoice is posted to the student ledger and to the general ledger, with the tax posted to its own account rather than folded into fee income.
Every invoice in the run is linked to one batch, so the whole run can be traced and reversed as a unit.
Each guardian has been sent their invoice and can open and print the challan from it.
Students excluded from the run are listed with the reason rather than passed over silently.
Nothing was calculated by hand. Every figure came from the approved structure and the adjustments applied in their fixed order.

dataFields.name: Billing period
dataFields.validation: The month or term being billed. Within the open academic session, and not more than one period ahead.

dataFields.name: Issue date
dataFields.validation: Not in the future, and not before the session start.

dataFields.name: Due date
dataFields.validation: On or after the issue date. Overdue tracking and any further late fee run from it.

dataFields.name: Remarks
dataFields.validation: Maximum 250 characters. Printed on the invoice.

dataFields.name: Structure amount
dataFields.validation: The first figure in the calculation, taken from the approved structure effective for the period (BR-2, BR-3).

dataFields.name: Concession
dataFields.validation: Deducted second. From the student's approved concession, up to its remaining balance (BR-4).

dataFields.name: Credit applied
dataFields.validation: Deducted third. From any credit balance held against the family code, so a sibling's credit reduces this bill (BR-5).

dataFields.name: Installment share
dataFields.validation: Applied fourth. The portion of the net due for this period under an approved plan (BR-6).

dataFields.name: Late fee carried
dataFields.validation: Added fifth. Late fee already accrued and not yet billed, carried onto this invoice as its own line (BR-7).

dataFields.name: Withholding tax
dataFields.validation: Added last. Only where the household has crossed the configured threshold (BR-8).

dataFields.name: Net payable
dataFields.validation: What the family owes for the period, after the full calculation.

dataFields.name: Invoice number
dataFields.validation: Unique per branch and academic session, gapless, never reused (BR-13).

dataFields.name: Batch number
dataFields.validation: Groups every invoice created in the run (BR-11).

businessRules.rule: Every amount is calculated. Nothing on an invoice is typed by the person raising it, and the fee type is not chosen here, having been set against the class in the approved structure.

The calculation follows one fixed order, and the order is part of the rule rather than an implementation detail: the structure amount, less concession, less credit held against the family code, split by any installment plan, plus late fee already accrued, plus withholding tax.
businessRules.formula: net = ((structure_amount − concession − credit_applied) × installment_share) + late_fee_carried + withholding_tax

businessRules.rule: The structure amount comes from the approved structure effective for the billing period. Where no approved structure covers the period, the student is excluded and listed rather than billed at a guess.
The concession is deducted before anything else, up to its remaining balance. It applies to the structure amount, so a family's discount is not eroded by a credit or inflated by a late fee.

Credit is held against the family code, not the student, so a credit arising from one child reduces a sibling's bill. It is applied after the concession, oldest credit first, and only up to the amount of the bill. It never takes an invoice below zero; the remainder stays held for the next one.
The installment split is applied to the net of structure less concession less credit, not to the structure amount. Splitting the gross would bill a family for a discount they had already been given.
Late fee already accrued and not yet billed is carried onto this invoice as its own line. It is added after the installment split, so a fine is never divided across installments.

Withholding tax is added last, and only where the household has crossed the configured threshold. It is assessed at family code level, not per student, and posts to its own tax account rather than to fee income.
A school-wide issue requires School Admin authorisation. Accounts may prepare and preview it, and the run holds until it is authorised.

Each adjustment appears as its own line on the invoice and on the challan. A family must be able to see the structure amount, what was taken off and what was added, rather than a single net figure they cannot check.
Every invoice in a run is linked to one batch, so the run can be traced afterwards and reversed as a unit.
Only students placed in a class and active on the issue date are billed. A student who has left, been struck off or not yet been placed is excluded.
Invoice numbers are gapless per branch and academic session and are never reused. A failed run consumes no numbers.
The same fee may not be billed twice to the same student for the same period. A repeat is excluded and listed; it does not abort the run.

The run is atomic per student. The invoice, its lines, the credit drawdown, the concession drawdown and the ledger postings are all created or none are, so a credit is never consumed by an invoice that failed to save.
An issued invoice is never edited. A wrong charge is cancelled if unpaid, or credited if paid, each through its own use case.

transitions.condition: A payment less than the net payable is recorded.
The debt is written off as uncollectable.
Scope is class, section or student.
The batch is reversed. Credit applied is returned to the family and paid invoices are refused and listed.

basicFlow.userAction: Chooses the scope: school-wide, one class, one section, or one individual student.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Loads the students in scope. The fee type is not chosen, having been set against the class in the approved structure.

basicFlow.navigation: Issue invoices → Billing period and due date
basicFlow.userAction: Enters the billing period and the due date.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks the period is within the open academic session and the due date is on or after the issue date.

Calculates each student's amount in the fixed order — structure amount, less concession, less family credit, split by installment plan, plus late fee accrued, plus withholding tax — and shows every adjustment as its own column.
For a school-wide scope, holds the batch for School Admin authorisation. Otherwise proceeds.

Creates each invoice with one line per fee component and one per adjustment, draws down the concession and the family credit, marks the carried late fee as billed, and posts to both ledgers, atomically per student.
Sends each invoice to every related parent at the point of creation, so they can open and print the challan.

basicFlow.userAction: Opens the batch to see what was created.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Shows every invoice in the run, the total billed, the credit applied, the tax withheld, and the students excluded with their reasons.

alternateFlows.behaviour: Nothing is created until the School Admin authorises. The preview is frozen so the run cannot change while it waits (BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: The family holds a credit balance from an earlier correction
alternateFlows.behaviour: The credit is applied after the concession, oldest first, up to the amount of the bill. It appears as its own line, the remainder stays held against the family code, and a credit arising from one child can reduce a sibling's bill (BR-5).

alternateFlows.condition: The student is on an approved installment plan
alternateFlows.behaviour: The split is applied to the net of structure less concession less credit, not to the structure amount, so the family is not billed for a discount they were already given (BR-6).

alternateFlows.condition: Late fee has accrued and has not yet been billed
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is carried onto this invoice as its own line, added after the installment split so a fine is never divided across installments (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: The household has crossed the withholding tax threshold
alternateFlows.behaviour: Tax is added last as its own line and posts to its own account rather than to fee income. The threshold is assessed at family code level, so several children in one household are counted together (BR-8).
The structure amount is the sum of the subjects the student actually takes, carried as one line per subject before any adjustment is applied (BR-3).

alternateFlows.condition: A whole run was raised in error
alternateFlows.behaviour: Every unpaid invoice in the batch is reversed as a unit, and any credit applied by the run is returned to the family code. Paid invoices are refused and listed, because money received is not undone by reversing a bill.

exceptions.condition: No approved fee structure covers the billing period
exceptions.systemResponse: Those students are excluded and listed. Nothing is billed at a guess (BR-3).
exceptions.messageShown: No approved structure covers Grade 4 for Sep 2026. Approve a structure before billing it.

exceptions.condition: The concession and the credit together exceed the structure amount
exceptions.systemResponse: The invoice is not taken below zero. The concession is applied in full, the credit only up to the balance, and the unused credit stays held against the family code (BR-5).

exceptions.condition: The withholding tax rate or the household threshold is not configured
exceptions.systemResponse: Those students are excluded rather than billed without the tax that is due on them (BR-8).
exceptions.messageShown: Withholding tax is not configured. Set the rate and threshold before issuing invoices for these households.

exceptions.condition: The billing period falls outside the open academic session
exceptions.messageShown: Select a period within the current academic session.

exceptions.condition: The due date is before the issue date
exceptions.messageShown: The due date must be on or after the issue date.

exceptions.systemResponse: Nothing is created; the batch goes for authorisation (BR-9).
exceptions.messageShown: A school-wide issue needs School Admin approval. The batch has been sent for authorisation.

exceptions.condition: A ledger posting fails for one student
exceptions.systemResponse: That student's invoice is rolled back entirely, including the credit and concession drawdowns, and the run continues. The student is listed as failed with the reason (BR-15).
exceptions.messageShown: X of Y invoices issued. Z could not be issued — see the batch detail.

exceptions.condition: Two runs draw on the same family credit at once
exceptions.systemResponse: The credit is drawn down once. The second run applies only what remains, so a credit is never spent twice (BR-5, BR-15).

exceptions.condition: Two users issue the same scope and period at once
exceptions.systemResponse: The second run finds the invoices already created and issues nothing (BR-14).
exceptions.messageShown: These invoices have already been issued in batch BATCH-2026-0091.

exceptions.condition: The invoice message to a guardian fails
exceptions.systemResponse: The invoice stands and the send is marked Failed. It can be resent. An invoice is never unmade because a message failed.
exceptions.messageShown: The invoices are issued. Some messages could not be sent — resend them from the batch.

acceptanceCriteria.given: Grade 4 with an approved structure of PKR 5,000 and 30 placed students
acceptanceCriteria.when: Accounts issue invoices for Sep 2026 at class scope
acceptanceCriteria.then: 30 invoices exist at PKR 5,000 each and the batch total is 150,000

acceptanceCriteria.given: A student with a structure amount of 5,000, a 1,000 concession, a 500 family credit, a plan billing half, an accrued late fee of 200 and tax of 88

acceptanceCriteria.then: the structure amount, the concession, the credit applied, the installment share, the late fee and the tax are each a separate line, not one combined figure

acceptanceCriteria.given: A family holding PKR 500 credit from a correction against their eldest child
acceptanceCriteria.when: the youngest child's invoice is raised
acceptanceCriteria.then: the credit reduces that invoice, because credit is held against the family code and not the student

acceptanceCriteria.given: A family holding PKR 6,000 credit against a bill of PKR 4,000
acceptanceCriteria.then: PKR 4,000 of credit is applied, the invoice is not taken below zero, and PKR 2,000 remains held for the next bill

acceptanceCriteria.given: A student with a 1,000 concession and a plan billing half
acceptanceCriteria.then: the split is applied to 4,000 and not to 5,000, so the family is not billed for a discount they were already given

acceptanceCriteria.given: A student with an accrued late fee of PKR 200 on a plan billing half
acceptanceCriteria.then: the full 200 appears, not 100, because a fine is added after the split and is never divided

acceptanceCriteria.given: A household with three children that has crossed the tax threshold
acceptanceCriteria.then: tax is assessed at family code level rather than per student, and posts to its own account rather than fee income

acceptanceCriteria.given: Two runs drawing on the same family credit at the same moment
acceptanceCriteria.then: the credit is drawn down once and the second run applies only what remains

acceptanceCriteria.given: A ledger posting that fails for one student
acceptanceCriteria.then: that student has no invoice and their concession and family credit are undrawn, and every other student is billed
no invoice exists, the batch is awaiting authorisation, and the School Admin has been notified

departures.requirement: A school-wide run of 5,000 students completes within 60 seconds and reports progress while it runs, including the credit and tax assessments.
A preview for a class of up to 60 students renders within 3 seconds with every adjustment column calculated.
The order of adjustments is fixed and identical in preview and in issue. A preview figure and the invoice raised from it must never differ.
A family credit is drawn down exactly once, even under concurrent runs across siblings in different classes.
Invoice numbers stay gapless under concurrent runs, and a failed run consumes none.
Invoices, their adjustment lines and their ledger postings are retained 7 years and are never hard-deleted.

openQuestions.question: Is credit applied automatically at every issue, or only when the office chooses to apply it?
openQuestions.assumption: Automatically, per the workflow. A family may prefer to hold it, and nothing currently lets them.

openQuestions.question: Where a family holds credit and several children are billed in one run, which child's invoice is it applied to first?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. Oldest invoice first is assumed, but the order changes which sibling's bill it reduces.

openQuestions.question: Is the installment split a fixed fraction or a schedule of stated amounts?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and rounding differs between the two.

openQuestions.question: Should the tax threshold be assessed on the household's billed fees for the year, or for the period?
openQuestions.assumption: For the year to date. Not confirmed, and it decides when a household crosses.

openQuestions.question: Where a late fee is carried onto a new invoice, does it stop accruing on the original one?
openQuestions.assumption: Yes, it is marked as carried. Not confirmed, and double-charging is the risk.

openQuestions.question: May an invoice be raised for a student placed part way through a period, and is it pro-rated?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and it decides what a mid-month admission is billed.

openQuestions.question: What is the default gap between issue date and due date?

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: bulk-actions
conventionsApplied.rule: Any bulk operation reports a per-row result, commits valid rows and lists rejected rows with the reason. A bulk action never fails as a whole because of one bad row.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
